questions.enonce_markdown: Why do we preserve food? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. To **prevent spoilage** by killing microorganisms or preventing their growth.
2. To **make food last longer** (increase shelf life).
3. To keep a **supply of food during times of scarcity** (dry season, famine), as seasonal foods are stored for later.
4. To **prevent food poisoning** and food-borne diseases.
5. To **retain the nutritive value**, taste and appearance of food.
6. To **reduce food wastage** and to allow food to be transported over long distances and sold.

(Any five.)

questions.enonce_markdown: How is food preserved by (i) Smoking (ii) Pasteurization? *(3, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Smoking**: meat or fish is hung or placed on racks above a wood fire and exposed to hot smoke for a long time. The heat **dries the food** (removes water) and the smoke deposits chemicals (for example phenols and formaldehyde) that **kill microorganisms or prevent their growth** and give a special flavour.

(ii) **Pasteurization**: food, mainly milk, is heated to about **63 $^\circ\mathrm{C}$ for 30 minutes** (or about 72 $^\circ\mathrm{C}$ for 15 seconds) and then **cooled rapidly**. This kills the disease-causing bacteria (for example the tuberculosis bacterium) without changing the taste and nutritive value of the food.

questions.enonce_markdown: How can food be contaminated at home? *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. By **flies, cockroaches and rats**, which carry germs on their bodies and feed on uncovered food.
2. By **dirty hands** of people handling or serving food (not washed after the toilet).
3. By **dirty utensils and surfaces** (plates, knives, chopping boards, kitchen tables).
4. By using **contaminated water** to wash or cook food.
5. By **coughing or sneezing** over food.
6. By **poor storage** (leaving food uncovered or keeping raw and cooked food together).
7. By **domestic animals** such as dogs, cats and chickens.

(Any four.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Name three examples of food-borne diseases and their respective causative agents. *(3, 3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Food-borne disease | Causative agent |
|---|---|
| **Cholera** | *Vibrio cholerae* (bacterium) |
| **Typhoid fever** | *Salmonella typhi* (bacterium) |
| **Bacillary dysentery** | *Shigella* species (bacterium) |

Other examples: amoebic dysentery (*Entamoeba histolytica*, a protozoan), food poisoning (*Staphylococcus aureus*), hepatitis A (a virus), taeniasis (tapeworm *Taenia saginata* or *Taenia solium*).
